solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Powdered earth?

definitions.meaning: crushed into powder, as coffee beans are

explanation.surface: A query about whether a heap of fine dust is simply soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: past participle of grind (milled fine) and the noun for soil or terrain.

clue.text: Importance of last king taking on a mission to get rid of king

indicators.note: the cypher takes the next letter on board, holding it within

parts.note: George VI was Britain's most recent king, and his royal cypher is GR VI

indicators.note: signals that the following piece is removed from the mission word

parts.note: a mission is a task
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A grand-sounding phrase about the significance of a final monarch embarking on a quest to depose another king.
explanation.walkthrough: George VI was the last British king before the present queen, and royal cyphers combine GR (Georgius Rex) with the regnal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas is weighty seriousness of manner, which lends a person importance or dignity.

clue.text: Scots know to carry two bloody types of wood

parts.note: O is one of the blood groups
A is another of the blood groups
ken is the Scottish verb for know

explanation.surface: Scots who know how to carry two gruesome kinds of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Two blood groups, O and A, come before Scottish KEN; 'to carry' is linking padding. Blood groups are A, B, AB and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning made from oak, so descriptive of timber in general terms.

clue.text: New York district representative returned? Don't bet on it!

parts.note: NoHo is the Manhattan area north of Houston Street

indicators.note: sent back, so the short word is read from its end

explanation.surface: A Manhattan politician seeking re-election: the punter advises against backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns REP to PER. 'returned' also suggests an election result, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone certain to fail is not worth a wager, so the exclamation describes such a person.

clue.text: Too American? American's great!

parts.note: swell is American slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Is this also American? An American's cheerful reply that it's wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in addition or also, an exact synonym in ordinary use.

clue.text: Junk trader's starting price in London hit hard

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial aitch, so the word loses its H

parts.note: to hammer something is to hit it hard

explanation.surface: A scrap merchant's opening price in the capital gets heavily punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in London' drops the H of HAMMER, as a Cockney would, leaving AMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sender of unwanted bulk email deals in electronic junk, so is a trader in rubbish.

clue.text: Fit for purpose, therefore without amplification?

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
no microphone, with mic as the short form

explanation.surface: A speaker reasoning that, lacking a microphone, the arrangement is suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic design suits the user and task efficiently, which is a form of being well suited to use.

clue.text: Fish coming up change course, turning to get room for manoeuvre

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: a turning word is read the other way round

parts.note: to yaw is to swing off course

explanation.surface: A fish surfaces and swerves, needing space to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' gives LEE from EEL; 'turning' gives WAY from YAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is slack or freedom of action, room to operate.

clue.text: Get down to business at post-summit dance

indicators.note: Latin post means after, so the dance follows the meeting

parts.note: a summit is a set of high-level talks
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Diplomats turn serious at the party after a summit meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is to discuss one's work, especially socially, which is an idiom for business conversation.

clue.text: (Relative — male/female one)

parts.note: a parent is a relative
he is the male pronoun
sis is a female sibling

explanation.surface: A bracketed aside noting a family member, either a man or woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue sits in brackets, so the bracketed remark itself is what is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthetical remark is an aside placed within brackets, exactly how this clue is printed.

clue.text: Line manager who'll need more than one line?

definitions.text: Line manager who'll need more than one line?

parts.words: Line manager who'll need more than one line?
parts.note: an office boss is recast as someone handling fishing line, needing several casts

explanation.surface: An office supervisor who requires several subordinates.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman manages a rod and line, and may need several lines to land a catch.

clue.text: Baker and lecturer in relationship

indicators.note: places the abbreviation inside the family word

parts.note: kin means family relationship

explanation.surface: A baker and an academic are romantically involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is an oven for firing pottery, so it bakes clay.

clue.text: Newish EU member's half-back containing another — man of the match?

indicators.note: the reversed half holds the second country within it
the half is read backwards
only the first half of the country's name is kept

parts.note: Cyprus joined the European Union in 2004
Romania, another recent EU member, joined in 2007

explanation.surface: A footballer from a recent EU country, playing half-back, marks an opponent and wins the match award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-back' reads like the football position but splits into two instructions: keep half the name, then turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebug compulsively plays with matches, so is a man of matches in a punning sense.

clue.text: Gatecrasher preparing to fry old lamb?

parts.note: battering food coats it in batter before frying
a ram is a grown male sheep, a lamb grown old

explanation.surface: An uninvited guest coating mutton for the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy beam used to break through gates and doors literally crashes gates.

clue.text: Showed partiality, excessively, and kissed with abandon

parts.note: too means to excess

indicators.note: wildly and without restraint, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone played favourites by kissing too much and too wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking sides means favouring one party in a dispute, which is bias.

clue.text: It's not clear this bit hasn't been dyed

definitions.meaning: an ill-defined matter, neither one thing nor another
a patch of hair left its natural silver colour

explanation.surface: Someone at the hairdresser unsure whether a patch was missed by the colourist.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambiguous zone between categories, and literally a region of hair gone silver.

clue.text: Unofficially, not hitting top form

definitions.meaning: falling short of one's best performance, a personal best being a record

explanation.surface: A sportsperson admits privately they are off their best.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidential remark is made privately; read literally, the phrase means below one's best mark.

clue.text: Victim of Winterman's predecessor?

definitions.meaning: a scapegoat or dupe who takes the blame
autumn comes before winter, and fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure called Winterman was preceded by someone who suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe set up to take the blame; punningly, an autumn chap who comes before a winter one.

clue.text: Revise futurism's leading part in Soviet art movement

parts.note: red describes Soviet communism

indicators.note: the leading letter goes inside the rearranged word
an art movement, but here the letters move about
the first letter of the word leads it

explanation.surface: Revising the role of futurism in a Soviet artistic school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' rearranges ART as RAT, and 'in' puts F, the 'leading part' of futurism, inside it to make RAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft a document is to write a new version, so to revise it.

clue.text: Merry because man's around

indicators.note: the name goes around the short word

parts.note: Joe is a man's name
cos is short informal because

explanation.surface: Cheerful because a man is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and humorous, close to jolly.

clue.text: Out of date, like one who got into rock ages ago?

definitions.meaning: antiquated and set in old ways

definitions.text: like one who got into rock ages ago?
definitions.meaning: a creature preserved in stone; surface suggests an old rock music fan

explanation.surface: Mocking an ageing fan who took up rock music decades ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas grown rigid and outdated are compared to ancient remains turned to stone.

clue.text: Jack up sound beams

indicators.note: the clue says to take the word as heard, not as written

parts.note: to jack up is to raise

explanation.surface: Lift the volume of sound beams, like a technician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like part of 'sound beams' but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are narrow beams of light or energy.

clue.text: Bird with beak of gold flying up

indicators.note: in a down entry, the pieces read upwards

parts.note: a nib is a bird's beak
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A bird with a golden bill rises into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a common garden songbird.

clue.text: Spooner's one cornering spot market, perhaps in fast food

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of paired words

parts.note: a dot is a spot
a hog takes everything for itself, as one cornering a market does

explanation.surface: A trader corners a commodities market, perhaps dealing in quick meals.
explanation.walkthrough: A dot hog is someone cornering the spot market; swapping D and H gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter in a bun is a classic snack sold for quick eating.

clue.text: Stick knife in one who's breaking writers' strike?

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to put a blade into its sheath
a strikebreaker poet: scab plus bard

explanation.surface: A striking writer wants to stab the colleague crossing the picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath holds a sword or dagger; the verb means to sheathe the blade.

clue.text: South Africa initially has recorded more than one try

indicators.note: a recording reproduces the spoken sound, so the letters are heard

parts.note: the first letters of South Africa, then 's for has

explanation.surface: South Africa's rugby side has scored several tries.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as letter names, S, A and 's sound like the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, so several attempts are plural efforts.

clue.text: Southern African state's lost national independence anthem's first verse

indicators.note: the following letters go missing from the country's name

parts.note: Tanzania is an East African country

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An African state lost its independence anthem's opening verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes N, I and A from the end of TANZANIA, leaving TANZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a section of a poem.
